strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: workspace.write can propose and proposal.apply can execute one approved patch_file hunk for an existing regular UTF-8 workspace file.

Patch apply requires WriteWorkspace permission, current unconsumed approval, expected target hash, fresh preflight, safe path validation, symlink rejection, and single-context matching before mutation.
Proposal and apply evidence stores bounded hunk count and hunk fingerprint, not raw hunk text, raw file content, raw diffs, absolute paths, environment, or secrets.
A headless caller can apply a small approved edit without replacing an entire file and can recover deterministically from stale hash, duplicate context, or authorization failures.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: One authorized proposal.apply call can atomically apply one approved patch_file single hunk to an existing regular UTF-8 file.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: replace_file requires supplying and approving full replacement content; create_file and delete_file do not support bounded in-place edits.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie would still require whole-file replacement for small edits, increasing review burden and raw-content handling pressure for headless workspace mutation.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M24.2 recovered partial delete transactions; M24.1 executed delete transactions; M23.2 recovered create transactions. This phase adds a new single-file patch operation.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends existing workspace.write proposal generation and proposal.apply execution.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This reuses existing proposal, preflight, apply result, and ledger evidence surfaces with hunk metadata.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime validates patch_file old/new hunk input, records a hunk fingerprint, checks the approved hunk at apply time, rejects duplicate or missing context, performs atomic replacement, and verifies post-write SHA-256.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can execute small approved workspace mutations with deterministic stale-target and context-mismatch failure behavior.
answers.milestone_progress: This opens M25 with the first controlled patch apply capability and establishes the single-hunk safety boundary for later patch expansion.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M25.1 must be reviewed for actual patch_file mutation behavior, hunk fingerprint binding, duplicate context rejection, expected hash validation, atomic replacement, post-write verification, and bounded evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M25.1 changes the current phase manifest only; guard engine changes are not expected.

exit_criteria: workspace.write accepts operation=patch_file with workspace-relative path, old_text, new_text, no content, and bounded hunk size
patch_file proposals validate an existing regular non-symlink UTF-8 target and require old_text to match exactly once
Proposal evidence stores hunk_count and hunk_fingerprint without raw hunk text or raw file content
proposal.apply accepts approved current unconsumed patch_file proposals through the existing RPC only
Apply requires authorize=true, expected_target_sha256, patch_old_text, patch_new_text, latest preflight, safe path, regular non-symlink UTF-8 target, and approved hunk metadata match
Missing, duplicate, stale, sensitive, hash-mismatched, unsupported, unauthorized, or permission-denied patch apply attempts do not mutate the workspace or consume authorization
Successful apply writes through the existing temporary sibling and atomic replacement path, verifies post-write SHA-256, consumes authorization, and records bounded apply result evidence
Ledger and RPC results do not expose raw file content, raw diffs, raw hunk text, prompts, provider responses, stdout/stderr, environment, secrets, absolute paths, or canonical paths
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M25.1 merges, continue M25 only for a distinct patch execution capability such as stale-context recovery or bounded multi-hunk admission; do not add report, history, digest, preview, or inspection-only wrappers.
